newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Daewoo, Korean Telecom bid in Uzbekistan.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo, Korean Telecom bid in Uzbekistan.

text.p: Uzbekistan named South Korea's Daewoo Telecom Co Ltd and Korean Telecom as priority candidates for setting up a $105 million joint venture to modernise Tashkent's telephone system, a telecommunications ministry official said on Tuesday.
The two Korean companies top a list of eight companies, divided into four groups, with which the government will negotiate on the venture.

The order of the groups represents the order the Uzbek government will follow in discussing the venture, if it fails to reach agreement with partners which are higher on the list, the official told Reuters.
1. Daewoo Telecom and Korean Telecom (South Korea)
Talks with the Korean companies will start in several days, the official said.
The tender for the right to form the joint venture, where a foreign partner will hold a 49 percent stake, will take place in November.
The joint venture, where the Uzbekistan Telecommunications Ministry and the state-owned Uztelekom will represent the Uzbek side, will run for 15 years.
Under the terms of the project, foreign investors are to modernise 350,000 telephone lines and build not less than 100,000 new ones within two to three years.

The foreign partner is also to replace mechanical exchanges for digital ones, instal optic-fibre lines between stations, set up management and information centres and to introduce seven-digit numbers.
Tashkent telephone network currently has 440,000 lines.
Funding for the project will come from a 12.7 billion yen credit provided by Japan's Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund in June last year.
Old Soviet-era telephones in the desert nation of 22 million make it a challenge even to place calls within the capital Tashkent.
The authorities are running a series of tenders to modernise telecoms infrastructure in Uzbekistan.
